messages:
Morgan: Heads-up — FinCo POC signed the SOW for a 6-week pilot. They want guidance on capacity for the enterprise commit discussion tomorrow. Customer peak traffic they shared: 12,000 req/min peak (burst to 18k/min), mix ~80% chat gen, 20% embedding batches. Avg output ~80 tokens, p95 latency target 300ms. Asking: how many reserved GPUs, autoscale policy, and pricing delta for reserved vs hosted?
Priya: Can we get the traffic shape? p50/p95 request sizes and token distribution? Also need to know embedding batch size + frequency. Without that our estimates will be fuzzy.
Morgan: They sent a sample profile in the drive link (private): https://redwood.internal/finco/poc/profile — quick summary from their CSV: median tokens 45, mean 80, 99th 420, embedding jobs: 1k calls/hour, each 256-dim (batch size 128).
Alex: Quick back-of-envelope for model "llama-13b-quant" fp16-ish perf: assume ~25k tokens/s per GPU under steady-state. At 200 rps * 80 tokens => ~16k tokens/s sustained. So 1 reserved GPU covers steady, but add headroom + canary = reserve 2 GPUs for predictability. Autoscale: min=1, target=2 (reserved), max=4 for spikes; configure burst credits to allow short bursts up to 3x for 5 minutes.
Priya: +1 for 2 reserved. For P99 latency and 300ms SLO we should recommend prewarm (hot KV cache) on both reserved GPUs and keep a warm standby. Also suggest a cheaper fallback model (7B quant) for overload — costs less tokens/sec and preserves availability.
Jared: Pricing question from FinCo — they asked what the delta is if they commit to 2 reserved GPUs vs using hosted at traffic levels. What's the simple line we can give them today for the call?
Priya: Ballpark: dedicated/reserved gives ~30-45% unit-cost reduction at steady high throughput vs pure hosted. Exact depends on model and quantization; reserved also removes multitenant variability which they care about. I'll prepare a short slide with 3 scenarios (hosted burst, 2-reserved + burst, 4-reserved runway).
Nina: Security flags — FinCo requires KMS with customer-managed keys, VPC-to-VPC peering for on-prem data, and SOC2 + vendor questionnaire completed. We still need to hand them the SQA. Morgan, can you confirm who owns questionnaire follow-up?
Morgan: I'll own the SQA follow-up. Action: I’ll send the filled questionnaire + network diagrams by EOD tomorrow.
AutoscaleBot: perf-sim-job-482 finished. Results: baseline sim at 200 qps, 10% jitter -> p95 latency 260ms, token throughput 16.8k/s, simulated GPU usage ~1.1 GPUs steady, spikes up to 3.2 GPUs. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/finco/sim/482
Alex: Good — sim aligns with the rough calc. Recommendation: reserved 2 GPUs, autoscale min=1, desired/reserved=2, max=4, prewarm cache on both, burst policy: allow 2x sustained for 10m then fall back to 7B. Canary rollout over 5% traffic for 30m before full cutover.
Jared: For the customer call, I'll say: "We recommend starting with 2 reserved GPUs + burst credits; we'll run a finetuned sim with your exact profile during the POC week and can convert to a 3/6/12-month reserved commit for better pricing once you hit stable throughput."
Priya: Also add note about embeddings — since they run 1k/hr (batch128), we can offload to a single CPU-backed worker for cheaper embedding throughput; this lowers GPU hours and cost.
Morgan: Next steps: (1) Priya to draft pricing scenarios and attach to the SOW (today), (2) Morgan to send SQA and network diagram (tomorrow EOD), (3) Alex to schedule perf-run on the dedicated pool with FinCo profile (slot booked Thu 10:00), (4) Jared to lead customer call Thurs 11:00. Anyone object?
Nina: No objections. I'll prep SOC2 vendor package and KMS integration checklist.
Jared: No objections. Going to run the pricing talk with the AE.
Morgan: Good. One more quick note — ask the customer if they need region affinity (they mentioned eu-west-1 preference). If yes, we should plan AZ fallback policy and potential cross-region replication costs.
Priya: I'll add region affinity to the checklist.
Morgan: Thanks all. I'll post the SOW + draft commit options after the call. :thumbsup:
